parts.label: (i)
parts.text:
Identify two economic policies the Uruguayan government has introduced that should
increase economic growth.

parts.label: (ii)
parts.text: Explain how these policies should increase Uruguay’s economic growth.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The information states that in Uruguay there is a national minimum wage.
Using a diagram, discuss the likely effects of the introduction of a national minimum wage on
labour markets.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Using Figs. 1.1 to 1.4, comment on the macroeconomic performance of Uruguay. 
Section B
Answer two questions.

text: Uruguay, a country of 3.5 million people, had a gross domestic product (GDP) per capita of
US$20 000 in 2017 and was ranked at 63 in the world.

efficiency.

parts.label: (b)

Using diagrams, discuss whether the policies employed by governments to reduce allocative
inefficiency are always effective.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain the roles of marginal costs and average costs in determining the profits of a firm.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Discuss whether mergers between firms always operate against the consumers’ interest.

text: The wages of the Chief Executive Officers (CEO) of the six largest banks in the United States
(US) were reported to be between 250 and 360 times the average wage of the workers in those
banks. The six CEOs were all male.
Discuss the extent to which economic theory can account for these variations in wages. [25]

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Analyse the causes of unemployment and explain which cause could be most significant for
your country.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Discuss whether supply-side policies are the most appropriate for reducing unemployment.

text: “Investment by multinational corporations (MNCs) in a developing country always promotes
sustainable economic growth in that country.”

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain why gross domestic product (GDP) is widely used as a measure of economic growth
and the standard of living.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Discuss why alternatives to GDP are increasingly used to measure the standard of living.
